summary: A command that has just sent a real POST/PUT/DELETE prints its response with source=live on every output path, never through the provenance-less printer whose "local" default is an assumption about unattributable data.
reason: printOutputWithFlags hardcodes source=local because it has nothing better to report, so any mutate command that prints through it is one output-mode change away from telling an agent that a playlist it just created on Spotify came from the local store — a claim the agent cannot check and would act on. Every mutate command already labels its JSON envelope live; the non-JSON fall-through must carry the same provenance so the two paths cannot disagree about where the same bytes came from.
validated_outcome: TestMutationCommandsDoNotPrintThroughProvenanceLessPrinter fails against the pre-fix source (it names any file that both issues a mutating client call and prints through printOutputWithFlags) and passes after. TestLiveMutationsReportLiveProvenance drives me create-playlist, me add-to-queue, me follow-artists-users, and playlists items add-to-playlist against an httptest server under --agent, asserts the request really went out, and pins meta.source == "live". go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l . clean. A follow-up in the same change added printJSONFilteredMeta and moved play-on's live-outcome call sites onto it: that was the one site where the "local" label was actually reachable under --agent, since the generated mutate commands never reach their provenance-less fall-through.
